Subject: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements — Acme Health

Hi Sarah / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the thoughtful conversation. Below is a short recap of what we heard, success criteria, and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Call recap (high level)
- Primary goal: deploy an LLM-based triage assistant for patient intake that does NOT store PII and provides traceable audit logs for compliance reviews.
- Pain points: current vendor keeps full transcripts (including PHI) and retention policies are unclear; lack of redaction and limited auditability for clinical QA.
- Current stack: Acme uses an on-prem data ingress pipeline -> Azure VNet -> existing NLP microservices. The pilot would need to sit behind your VPC with controlled egress.

Success criteria for pilot
1) All patient-identifying fields (PHI/PII) redacted before any persisted logs leave your VPC.
2) Audit logs that record request/response metadata (timestamp, model version, request id) and are exportable for 90 days.
3) Demonstrable retention and deletion workflows to support your legal/process audits.
4) Latency target: p95 < 350ms for single-turn triage on reserved capacity.

Questions / open items we agreed to follow up on
- Exact list of fields you want considered PII/PHI for automated redaction (please send the spreadsheet).
- Whether audit logs must include full request payloads or only metadata (your security team prefers metadata-only exports).
- Any regulatory requirements we should account for beyond HIPAA (e.g., state-level rules, internal policies).

Next steps
1) Marissa to send a short questionnaire (DPA + technical) and SOC2 summary — attached.
2) Acme to complete and return the DPA/questionnaire and redaction field list by Aug 6.
3) Redwood to provide a follow-up note from our security lead (cc'd) with details on audit logs, retention, and optional on-prem deployment patterns.
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/security team (suggest Aug 10 or 11).

Attachments: acme-data-processing-questionnaire.xlsx (please fill), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on another call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful and aligned. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- We will attach the list of PII/PHI fields; for the pilot please treat the following as required redactions: full name, DOB, SSN, phone, email, address, MRN (medical record number). We may add other free-text heuristics later.
- For audit logs: we prefer metadata-only exports (timestamp, request id, model version, redaction-status) but need the ability to replay full request payloads under a legal hold scenario. Is that possible with your platform, gated by customer-managed KMS and access controls?
- Retention: 90 days is our baseline for the pilot; longer-term we may require 1 year for specific audit trails.

Also looping in Tom (infra) — he prefers a technical deep-dive next week.

Thanks,
Sarah

Hi Sarah / Tom — thanks for the quick response and clear list.

Short answers to your questions (we'll follow up with Vivek's note with more detail):
- Replay under legal hold: yes — Redwood can be configured to keep encrypted full payload archives accessible only via customer-managed KMS and role-based access. We surface access logs and require an access justification audit when retrieving payloads.
- Metadata-only exports: supported out of the box; you can toggle full-payload archiving per-route.
- Retention window: pilot-configurable (90 days default). We can support 1 year for specific audit trails with dedicated retention buckets.

Hi Sarah / Tom — looping in a few details ahead of the technical deep-dive. Two pages of notes below and a sample audit log extract attached.

1) Redaction and PII handling- We support pre-processing redaction hooks that run inside the customer's VPC (on your infra or our private deployment) so PII can be redacted before it touches any persisted storage. Redaction is rule-based (regex) with optional ML-based PII detectors; customers can supply additional fields to redact.

2) Audit logs and retention- We emit structured audit logs that include: request_id, timestamp, model_version, route, redaction_status (boolean), truncated_metadata (size-limited).- Full request/response payloads are archived to encrypted buckets when enabled; access is gated with customer-managed KMS and require an RBAC approval workflow.- Export formats: CSV/JSON; we can stream to your SIEM or SFTP.

3) Deletion and legal hold- Deletion requests can be automated via API or manual from the Console. For legal holds, we support retention flags that prevent deletion and mark records as "frozen" until released.

4) Compliance artifacts- Attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, redwood-audit-logs-sample.csv. We can schedule a SOC2 evidence review with your audit team if helpful.

Next steps I recommend:
- Technical deep-dive (30–45m) with infra/security: propose Aug 10 @ 10:00am PT or Aug 11 @ 2:00pm PT.
- You send the final field list and completed questionnaire by Aug 6 so we can prepare an architecture diagram and config recommendations.

Thanks — happy to answer any follow-ups.

-Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
